clue.text: Composer has intros to set your partner alight!

indicators.note: partner says the intros join up with, and follow, the word for alight

parts.note: to debus is to get off a bus, so to alight

indicators.note: intros to the words that follow are their opening letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to set fire to your other half, with a composer's name attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alight' looks like 'on fire' beside 'set', but it means getting off a vehicle: DEBUS. The intros (first letters) of 'set your' give SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was the French composer of La Mer and Clair de Lune.

clue.text: Humble beginnings in dead-end English backwater are so embarrassing

indicators.note: beginnings in the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Coming from a dead-end English backwater is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' is a verb here: to debase someone is to humble them.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to lower in status or dignity, to humble.

clue.text: In Ireland my gold is stashed in converted barge

indicators.note: is stashed in says the heraldic gold is hidden away inside the reworked barge
converted says the letters of barge are rearranged

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Irish gold hidden in a converted canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges barge to BEGRA; 'is stashed in' places the heraldic gold within it. 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Begorra is a stage-Irish exclamation like 'my!' or 'by God!', used in Ireland.

clue.text: Obeying this criminal command could be the making of me

definitions.text: Obeying this criminal command could be the making of me

parts.words: Obeying this criminal command could be the making of me
parts.note: a robber's order to raise the hands; read literally in a down entry, putting EM up turns it into me

explanation.definitionFit: Stick 'em up is the classic hold-up order, and 'em placed upwards reads as me.

clue.text: Posturing, I agree, holding work up

indicators.note: holding says the word for agreement goes round the reversed piece

parts.note: ya, a casual yeah, means I agree

indicators.note: up in a down entry says the word for work reads upwards

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing while striking a pose and keeping a job going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the verb for work to OG in this down entry, and 'holding' wraps the casual yes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a practice of holding bodily postures, so it is a kind of posturing.

clue.text: Abandon find

definitions.meaning: to ... a job or plan is to give it up
to ... evidence or results is to turn them up, bring them to light

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has both senses: giving something up, and producing or turning something up.

clue.text: Figure who turned corrupt, then died

indicators.note: corrupt says the letters of these words are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who went bad and then passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' is fodder, not a reversal: WHO TURNED rearranged gives TWOHUNDRE, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: Two hundred is a number, and a number is a figure.

clue.text: German poet's touching and kind at heart

indicators.note: at heart says the word for kind sits in the middle of the word for touching

parts.note: re means touching, concerning
ilk means kind or sort

explanation.surface: A German poet described as moving and kind deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was a German-language poet, author of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Kaiser's brief is to command

indicators.note: brief says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: will means is to, as in he will go, he is to go
the helm means control, command

explanation.surface: The emperor's whole job is to give orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a noun (instructions) but it cuts WILL to WIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm II was the last German Kaiser, so the name stands for a Kaiser.

clue.text: Asian people crush barrels

parts.note: a pash is a schoolgirl crush, an infatuation
tuns are large casks or barrels

explanation.surface: Asian workers crushing barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pashtuns are an ethnic group of Afghanistan and Pakistan.

clue.text: What's person without goods to get out?

definitions.text: What's person without goods to get out?

parts.words: What's person without goods to get out?
parts.note: a person with no possessions, a pauper, would bring out a vessel for alms; 'get out' reads as escape but means produce

explanation.definitionFit: A beggar holds out a bowl to collect coins, so it is what the destitute person takes out.

clue.text: Short boy or girl? Not so short

indicators.note: short says the word is cut off at its end

parts.note: less means not so, as in not so short is less short

explanation.surface: A question about a child's height, then a correction that the child is not that small.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Short' is part of the definition (a shortened name); the second is the instruction to cut the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Les is a pet form of Leslie or Lesley, names given to boys and girls alike.

clue.text: Songbird's cry with energy going to last

indicators.note: going to last says the letter for energy moves to the end of the word for cry

parts.note: a shriek is a loud cry
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A songbird's call that uses its energy right to the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: The E in SHRIEK moves to the end, giving SHRIKE; 'Songbird's' is the definition with 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrike is a perching songbird, the butcher-bird that impales its prey on thorns.

clue.text: Most unusual pursuit, having dated before being introduced at

indicators.note: being introduced says the archaic word is put inside the word for pursuit

parts.note: a quest is a search or pursuit
ere is an old-fashioned word for before

explanation.surface: A peculiar chase in which someone had already dated before being introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dated' marks 'before' as archaic, and 'being introduced' puts it into the pursuit. The closing 'at' reads as a link word in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer in its older sense means odd or strange, so the superlative means the most unusual.

clue.text: Old woman —— one abandoning bed after planting seed potato

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman

indicators.note: after planting says the seed has been put inside the riser

parts.note: a riser is one who gets up out of bed
a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: An old woman and an early riser planting seed potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after planting' means having put the seed inside the early riser. Maris Piper is a staple British potato variety, used for chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Maris Piper is a popular British variety of potato.

clue.text: Staff on hand master varied work

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it
varied says the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Staff working alongside a farmhand and a master in a mixed job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges hand master to ARMSANDTHE, and 'on' puts staff after it. Shaw's comedy is the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms and the Man is a comedy by Shaw, a theatrical work.

clue.text: Yokel making hay's inside poorly, note

indicators.note: making, with 'inside', says the middle letter of hay is turned into the following pieces

parts.note: hay taken as written
poorly means ill
a bill is a banknote

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin feeling unwell while haymaking, with a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making ... inside' says the middle letter of hay is turned into the following pieces, leaving the outer letters of hay around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillbilly is an unsophisticated person from remote country, a yokel.

clue.text: Grabbing at clothing button it, expressing disgust

indicators.note: clothing says the first word covers the call for silence

parts.note: pawing means grabbing at clumsily
sh is the call to be quiet, to button it

explanation.surface: Someone grabbing at clothes while being told to button it, and showing distaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' and 'button' suggest garments, but 'button it' means shut up, and 'clothing' means the grabbing word wraps round that call.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an exclamation of contempt, so pshawing is voicing disgust.

clue.text: DJ's spinning a record: over-st whelming fancy to stay out all 1 is night?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'DJ's spinning a record: over-st whelming fancy to stay out all 1 is night?' is OCR-garbled ('over-st whelming', '1 is'); the blog gives LIKE inside PEEL'S reversed + A LOG but not the clue's exact words.
annotationWithheld.clue: DJ's spinning a record: over-st whelming fancy to stay out all 1 is night?

clue.text: Retaining mass doesn't, strangely, last

indicators.note: retaining says the rearranged letters hold the letter for mass
strangely says the letters of doesn't are mixed up

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Something that keeps its mass, oddly, fails to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: DOESNT rearranged gives ENDOST, which holds M.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest along, at the very end, so last.

clue.text: Please check underneath edge of flooring

indicators.note: underneath in a down entry puts this piece below the edge letter
edge of the word means its final letter here

parts.note: to ratify is to confirm, loosely to check

explanation.surface: A request to inspect under the edge of the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' is the verb, not a polite request.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify someone is to please or satisfy them.

clue.text: Russian very great while wearing cap

indicators.note: wearing says the long period has the cap put on it, so sits inside

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat or cap
an eon is an immensely long period of time

explanation.surface: A Russian, very great, while putting on a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very great while' looks like praise plus 'while', but it is one phrase: EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonid is a common Russian man's name, like Leonid Brezhnev.

clue.text: Express back page succeeds with cartoon

parts.note: and means with, along with

indicators.note: back says the word for express is read in reverse

parts.note: pacy means fast, express

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper's back page succeeding thanks to its cartoon strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the Daily Express newspaper, but it is the adjective meaning fast, which 'back' turns to YCAP; 'succeeds' puts page after it, and 'with' leads the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Capp is the long-running British newspaper strip cartoon about a work-shy northern working-class man.

clue.text: English poet's mind something expanded by whisky, we hear!

parts.note: to mind is to care
whisky is W in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An English poet whose mind is said to grow with whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' refers to the radio alphabet's spoken code word; Thomas Carew was a 17th-century Cavalier poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carew was an English Cavalier poet of the court of Charles I.

clue.text: Burning tar to chill

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is an AB, an able seaman
to laze is to chill out, relax

explanation.surface: A sailor relaxing while something burns.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as read gives 'car', but the wordplay needs 'tar', the old word for a sailor, AB (able-bodied seaman).
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze means on fire, burning brightly.

clue.text: Turned up gas and stripped nude for shower

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry says the letters for gas read upwards

parts.note: CS gas is tear gas

indicators.note: stripped says the word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone turned the gas up, undressed and went to wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is not a wash but a sudden gust of rain or cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scud is a light passing shower or a driving cloud blown by the wind.

clue.text: Words made up, as performer admits?

definitions.meaning: A constructed international language, a set of invented words
someone asked whether they perform would admit it with the reply of two short words, an assent

explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial language made from Esperanto, and 'I do' is how a performer owns up to performing.

clue.text: Rogue strikes one, pinching ring and running

indicators.note: pinching says the word for ring is gripped inside the earlier pieces

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or strikes
I is the Roman numeral one
to ring someone is to call them
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A villain hits someone, stealing a ring and fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' places the phone word inside strikes plus one, just before the numeral, and running follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapscallion is a mischievous rascal or rogue.

clue.text: Start fighting, having fetched wide cutting blade

parts.note: got means fetched, as in went and got it

indicators.note: cutting says the letter for wide goes into the word for blade

parts.note: an oar's blade, so an oar is called a blade
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a broad sword and begins a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blade' suggests a sword, but here it is an oar; W (a wide in cricket, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to war is to begin hostilities, to start fighting.

clue.text: Bread's changed colour 'externally, unlike blubber

indicators.note: externally says the word for changed colour sits outside the bread

parts.note: dyed means changed in colour
rye is a type of bread

explanation.surface: A loaf that has turned a different colour on its crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' is not whale fat but someone who blubbers, cries; 'externally' says changed colour wraps round the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry-eyed means not weeping, the opposite of someone who blubbers.
